key_insight: Chimera shows that a hybrid diffusion transformer can scale to much larger visual contexts more efficiently than full-attention models. By mixing linear-time state tracking with latent attention, it aims to handle high-resolution images and long videos without the usual quadratic cost.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the compute and memory bottleneck of full attention in visual generation, especially for high-resolution images, long videos, and multimodal inputs where token counts become very large.
method: Uses a hybrid visual diffusion backbone that processes text, image, and video tokens in one raster-ordered stream.
Removes the need for positional embeddings by relying on stream-based token processing.
Combines Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for O(N) long-context state tracking with interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) to balance efficiency and expressiveness.
Applies a principled scaling recipe inspired by Chinchilla-style scaling to guide model design and training.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path to scaling visual generation models to richer inputs without exploding compute costs. For practitioners, Chimera suggests a more efficient architecture for building high-resolution image and video generators that can handle longer multimodal contexts.
